1.explanation:
All three files participate in how WebGL fills and clips polygon rings:  
1. MixedGeometryBatch.js  
   • Flattens and batches polygon rings and invokes the ring-orientation test to distinguish outer vs. hole rings before triangulating or stencil-masking.  
2. VectorStyleRenderer.js  
   • Drives the WebGL draw call for polygon fills using stencil operations. If outer and hole rings are mis-identified (clockwise logic inverted), holes won’t mask out properly.  
3. utils.js  
   • Contains helper routines (e.g. winding or orientation checks) used by the batcher and style renderer.  
Together these control how polygon rings are interpreted, triangulated, and composited in WebGL; an inversion or misuse of the clockwise test here leads directly to overlapping fills instead of punched-out holes.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering a GeoJSON polygon with holes in a WebGL vector layer, the fill-color is drawn multiple times (rings overlap) instead of creating a true cut-out for the hole. In the screenshots you can see a darkened solid fill where a ‘reversed zone’ (everything but the hole) should be transparent. The issue only appears under the WebGL renderer when the GeoJSON rings have the correct clockwise orientation; if the rings are (invalidly) reversed, the hole is drawn correctly. The old Canvas/VectorLayer implementation never had this problem.

2.explanation:
• src/ol/geom/flat/orient.js  – defines the winding‐order tests (signed area) used throughout the library. If its orientation convention doesn’t match the WebGL pipeline, holes and exteriors get misclassified.  
• src/ol/geom/flat/flip.js    – contains logic to reverse ring winding. It’s invoked (directly or indirectly) when enforcing a default orientation, but the default expected by WebGL is currently inverted relative to GeoJSON.  
• src/ol/geom/Polygon.js      – the geometry class that flattens and may reorient exterior and interior rings on construction. Incorrect defaults here propagate bad ring orders to the renderer.  
• src/ol/render/webgl/utils.js – helper routines for converting flat coords into WebGL buffers. It doesn’t apply even‐odd fill or hole subtraction, so it relies entirely on correct winding to cull inner rings.  
• src/ol/render/webgl/MixedGeometryBatch.js – batches and triangulates rings for WebGL. It treats every ring as a full polygon if the winding test misclassifies a hole, leading to filled inner rings.  
• src/ol/render/webgl/VectorStyleRenderer.js – orchestrates geometry instructions for WebGL fill. It assumes holes have the opposite winding to exteriors; with the spec‐correct GeoJSON winding the assumption is flipped and holes are rendered as solid fills.
2.bug_scenario: When rendering GeoJSON polygons with holes (an outer ring and one or more interior rings) using the WebGL vector layer, the fill‐color is applied not only to the outer ring but also to the interior rings. Valid GeoJSON (which uses CCW for the exterior and CW for holes) results in overlapping fill on the inner rings; if you deliberately reverse the ring winding (making the GeoJSON invalid), the issue disappears. This points to a misinterpretation of ring orientation and hole subtraction in the WebGL renderer.
